guide_enrichment.narrative:
For us, the case for Maryland starts with a passing game that can stay on schedule even if the rushing attack remains inefficient. Malik Washington has completed 53 of 72 passes for 533 yards without an interception, while Maryland has converted 55.2 percent of its third downs and has yet to commit a turnover. We are not assuming those rates will continue unchanged, but they support our model’s view that Maryland can create enough scoring opportunities against a Virginia Tech defense that has struggled to prevent them.

The main challenge is Virginia Tech’s ability to disrupt that rhythm. Virginia Tech leads the FBS with 12 sacks through two games, so Maryland cannot count on another clean, highly efficient passing performance. Still, our disagreement with the market is driven more by Maryland’s offensive path and overall matchup profile than by its recent results alone. We see enough ways for Maryland to move the ball and finish drives to support our position.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Virginia Tech’s rushing offense against Maryland’s rush defense. Our efficiency numbers identify this as Virginia Tech’s clearest advantage, and Overton Jr. has already rushed for 151 yards at 6.57 yards per carry with two touchdowns. Maryland has allowed only 38.5 rushing yards per game through two weeks, but our longer-run view is less convinced by that early surface number. If Maryland limits efficient runs and keeps Virginia Tech out of favorable down-and-distance situations, we think the matchup shifts toward the side of the ball that best supports our wager.

recent_game.fact: Maryland improved to 2-0 with a 38-14 road win over UConn on Sept. 12.
Maryland outgained UConn 475-223, recorded 27 first downs and held the ball for 35:31.
Maryland completed 35 of 42 passes for 350 yards without an interception against UConn.
Maryland rushed 36 times for 125 yards and three touchdowns against UConn.
Maryland held UConn to 67 rushing yards, 156 passing yards and 12 first downs while recording five sacks.
Maryland produced scoring drives of 92 and 91 yards in the second quarter against UConn, its first game with multiple 90-yard drives since 2018.

opponent_notes.fact: Virginia Tech enters the matchup 2-0 overall and 0-0 in the ACC.
Virginia Tech quarterback Grunkemeyer has completed 48 of 62 passes for 551 yards and four touchdowns through two games.
Virginia Tech running back Overton Jr. has rushed for 151 yards at 6.57 yards per carry with two touchdowns.
Virginia Tech receiver Reynolds has 13 receptions for 158 yards and three touchdowns.
Virginia Tech leads the FBS with 12 defensive sacks through its first two games.

quarterback.fact: Maryland starting quarterback Malik Washington is 53-of-72 for 533 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions through two games.
Washington completed 34 of 41 passes for 347 yards and two touchdowns against UConn.
Washington set a Maryland record by completing 18 consecutive passes against UConn; his 82.9 percent completion rate was the fourth-best single-game mark in program history.
Washington started all 12 games as a true freshman in 2025 and passed for 2,963 yards and 17 touchdowns.
Backup quarterback Cardell Williams completed four of five passes for 60 yards and a touchdown and rushed five times for 49 yards against Hampton.

offensive_personnel.fact: Maryland's offensive line starters against UConn were left tackle Rahtrel Perry, left guard Amory Hills, center Michael Hershey, right guard Ryan Howerton and right tackle Isaiah Wright.
Amory Hills made his first Maryland start at left guard against UConn after transfer Tellek Lockette started the opener there.
Rahtrel Perry has made 39 consecutive career starts, the most among Maryland offensive players.
Na'eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding, a transfer from Old Dominion, has 14 receptions for 187 yards and two touchdowns through two games.
Gladding recorded eight receptions for 130 yards and a touchdown against UConn.
Chris Durr Jr., a transfer from Wyoming, recorded 10 receptions for 106 yards and a touchdown against UConn.
Running back Harry Dalton III, a transfer from USC, rushed for career highs of 48 yards and two touchdowns against UConn.
Iverson Howard has rushed for 121 yards and three touchdowns through two games, including 55 yards and a touchdown against UConn.
Maryland returned starting quarterback Malik Washington, tight end Dorian Fleming and running back DeJuan Williams from its 2025 offense.

defensive_personnel.fact: Maryland's listed defensive starters against UConn included Lavon Johnson, Eyan Thomas, Nahsir Taylor, Sidney Stewart, Trey Reddick, Daniel Wingate, Jamare Glasker, Amari Jackson, Jordan Scruggs, Messiah Delhomme and Lavain Scruggs.
Sidney Stewart recorded six tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, one sack and a forced fumble against UConn.
Derrick LeBlanc, a transfer from UCF, recorded two sacks against UConn, his first two sacks for Maryland.
Freshman linebacker Zion Elee recorded his first career sack and forced a fumble against UConn; DD Holmes recovered the fumble.
DD Holmes leads Maryland with 2.5 sacks, while Eyan Thomas and Derrick LeBlanc each have two through two games.
Daniel Wingate, Maryland's 2025 leading tackler with 102 tackles, has made 26 consecutive defensive starts.
Maryland added defensive linemen Lavon Johnson from Texas, Derrick LeBlanc from UCF, and Armon Parker and Jayvon Parker from Washington through the transfer portal.
Transfer defensive backs Amari Jackson and Jordan Scruggs both started against UConn and each recorded four tackles.

coaching_changes.fact: Virginia Tech is in its first season under head coach James Franklin.
Clint Trickett became Maryland's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach during the offseason after serving as Jacksonville State's offensive coordinator in 2025.
Matt Barnes became Maryland's special teams coordinator after spending the previous two seasons at Mississippi State.
Maryland hired Randy Starks to coach the defensive line and Kyle Schmitt to coach the tight ends.
